entry.for_place: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán (area ca. 1905–1915)

jurisdictions.name: Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacan, Mexico

collections.title: Mexico, Michoacán and Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996

quirks: The municipality of Múgica was not created until February 12, 1942. For the 1905–1915 period, Nueva Italia (founded ca. 1909) fell under predecessor jurisdiction — most likely Parácuaro or La Huacana. Search the statewide civil collection under Parácuaro, not Múgica.

No civil registration, church, or census records are available online for the municipality of Múgica per the FamilySearch Wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy).
Parácuaro parish (Asunción, 1838–1967) and civil registration (1881–1931) are available at FamilySearch Catalog and are the closest documented records to Nueva Italia for this period.

Civil registration in Mexico began nationally in 1859 but was not strictly enforced until 1867; compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920). Church records are often more complete for this window.

The family was mobile across the Michoacán-Guerrero border. Because the siblings were born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, search both states' collections simultaneously — Mauro may also have been born in Guerrero.

Mexican naming system: children take the father's first surname and the mother's first surname. 'Cruz' is the paternal surname; 'Corona' is the maternal surname. Index searches should prioritize 'Cruz' as the family name.

Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (1637–1915) are at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog/320251) and may document parents' or grandparents' marriages predating civil registration.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Michoacán, Mexico — Nueva Italia / Múgica Area (ca. 1905–1915)

See research notes for full guide text. Key findings: Múgica municipality did not exist before 1942; no records online for Múgica; search statewide Michoacán civil collection (FS collection 1916243) under Parácuaro; use Parácuaro Asunción parish records (catalog/162793, 1838–1967); also search statewide Catholic Church Records (FS collection 1883388). Civil registration at municipality level began 1859, enforcement from 1867. During the Revolution (1910–1920) church records are more reliable.

quirks: The Coahuayutla municipal civil registration catalog item begins only in 1921 (FamilySearch Catalog 819525). For the 1913–1918 sibling births, search the statewide Guerrero civil collection (FS collection 1918291, indexed + images) and browse under Coahuayutla.

San Agustín parish, Coahuayutla, recorded baptisms, marriages, and deaths 1819–1930 (FamilySearch Catalog 1037615). This is the primary church source for the 1905–1918 window; browse-only (not name-indexed as a standalone item).
The statewide Guerrero Catholic Church Records (FS collection 1823323) IS name-indexed and may include Coahuayutla San Agustín records — search by surname 'Cruz' in Coahuayutla first.
Civil registration compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920). For sibling births 1913–1918 specifically, church baptismal records are likely more complete than civil records.

Guerrero borders Michoacán to the north and west. The Cruz family was mobile across this border. Search La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca (Guerrero, adjacent coastal municipality) and Parácuaro (Michoacán) alongside Coahuayutla.

The FamilySearch Wiki for Guerrero Catholic Church Records notes: when a person cannot be found, 'consider looking at collections for surrounding localities — Michoacán is to the northwest' (source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Guerrero,_Catholic_Church_Records_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records).
Guerrero population ca. 1910: approximately 594,300 (Populstat). State capital: Chilpancingo de los Bravo. Guerrero admitted as state October 27, 1849.

# Locality Guide: Guerrero, Mexico — Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga (ca. 1905–1918)

See research notes for full guide text. Key findings: Statewide Guerrero civil collection (FS 1918291, 1.73M records indexed + images, 1860–1996) is primary civil source. Statewide Catholic Church Records (FS 1823323, 2.58M records indexed + images, 1576–1979) is primary church source. San Agustín parish Coahuayutla records specifically 1819–1930 at FamilySearch Catalog (1037615) — browse-only. Municipal civil catalog item begins only 1921 (catalog 819525). For sibling births 1913–1918, the Revolution suppressed civil registration; parish records are likely more complete. Cross-border searches in La Unión (Guerrero) and Parácuaro (Michoacán) also warranted.

entry.rationale: Mauro Cruz Corona (b. ca. 1910, Nueva Italia area, Michoacán) has three siblings — Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz — documented as born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1913–1918. Per Mexican naming convention (Mexico_Naming_Customs wiki; loc_001; loc_002): Cruz is the paternal surname and Corona is the maternal surname. This means the family patriarch's surname was Cruz and the matriarch's maiden (paternal) surname was Corona. Starting point: siblings' baptisms in Guerrero are the fastest path to both parents' names; Mauro's own baptism under Parácuaro (predecessor jurisdiction for Nueva Italia, per loc_001) is the direct answer to the birth-date-and-place sub-question. Civil registration compliance was suppressed during the Revolution (1910–1920), so church records are sequenced first for the birth window. The Michoacán collections_search returned 0 results (possible tool-scope limitation); plan items for Michoacán cite loc_001 data directly. The 1930 Mexico Census is the only major national census publicly available for this era and could capture Mauro with parents.

entry.rationale: The three siblings (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) are documented as born in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1913–1918. Their Catholic baptism records in FS collection 1823323 (Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, 1576–1979, name-searchable (personCount 21256598)) will name both parents. Per Mexican naming convention, baptism entries record the father's full two-surname name and the mother's full two-surname name — giving us both the paternal-line Cruz surname chain and the maternal Corona surname chain. Searching surname 'Cruz' filtered to Coahuayutla, 1908–1920, should surface all three siblings and potentially Mauro himself if born in Guerrero. This is the required FAN/sibling item for a parentage question and the highest-probability starting point. Per loc_002, the statewide collection is name-searchable and more complete than the San Agustín parish standalone catalog (1037615, browse-only). Note: also try variant 'Crus.'

entry.jurisdiction: Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga, Guerrero, Mexico
entry.rationale: Search FS collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860–1996, name-searchable (personCount 8406443)) for civil birth registrations of the Cruz siblings and Mauro himself in Coahuayutla, Guerrero, 1905–1920. Civil birth acts (actas de nacimiento) name both parents with full surnames. Per loc_002, compliance dropped sharply during the Revolution (1910–1920), so church records (pli_001) are sequenced first and are more likely to yield results for the sibling birth window. Mauro may also appear here if born in Guerrero rather than Michoacán. Quirk: the Coahuayutla municipal civil catalog begins only in 1921 (loc_002); use the statewide Guerrero collection 1918291, not the municipal catalog.

Dedicated parentage plan item: search FS collection 1823323 (Mexico, Guerrero, Catholic Church Records, name-searchable (personCount 21256598)) for the Catholic marriage of a Cruz man to a Corona woman in Guerrero, ca. 1895–1912. This record: (a) confirms the couple as a married unit; (b) supplies the mother's full name — given name + paternal surname 'Corona' + her own maternal surname — which census and death records almost never give; (c) by date relative to Mauro's ca. 1910 birth, corroborates a father named only by the sibling baptisms. Note: the marriage record proves the couple married — it is not by itself evidence that Mauro is their child; that link requires the baptism or civil birth record placing Mauro with these parents. Date window: upper bound set by Mauro's ca. 1910 birth (parents must have married before); lower bound ca. 1895, assuming parents born ca. 1875–1880 and marrying in their late teens or early twenties.

Search FS collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, name-searchable (personCount 8406443)) for the civil marriage of a Cruz man to a Corona woman in Guerrero, ca. 1895–1912. Civil marriage acts often name both parties' parents (making them equivalent to a birth record for the grandparents), supply each party's age, and record the exact date and place. Date window bounded by the same logic as pli_003: parents must have married before Mauro's ca. 1910 birth, so upper bound 1910; lower bound ca. 1895 assuming late-teen or early-twenties marriage. This item is a fallback for pli_003 in case the church marriage record is not found or is not indexed.

Search FS collection 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacán and Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996) for Mauro Cruz's baptism in Parácuaro, Michoacán, ca. 1907–1913. Per loc_001, Nueva Italia (founded ca. 1909) fell under Parácuaro jurisdiction for this period — Múgica municipality did not exist until February 12, 1942. Availability: collections_search returned 0 for Michoacán (possible tool-scope limitation); loc_001 confirms this collection covers the target period with images. Search under Parácuaro as the predecessor jurisdiction. A baptism record would name both parents and confirm Mauro's exact birth date and place, directly answering both parts of q_001. Also try Cruz variant 'Crus.' If the indexed search underdelivers, the Parácuaro Asunción parish records (FamilySearch Catalog 162793, 1838–1967) are available for a browse-only follow-up.

Search FS collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940) for Mauro Cruz's civil birth registration in Parácuaro, Michoacán, ca. 1907–1913. Per loc_001, Nueva Italia records fall under Parácuaro for this era. Availability: collections_search returned 0 for Michoacán scope; loc_001 reports this collection as indexed with images covering 1859–1940. Civil registration compliance was reduced during the Revolution (1910–1920), so this item is sequenced after the church record search (pli_005). The civil birth act (acta de nacimiento) names both parents and records the exact date and place of birth — directly answering both parts of q_001. This item falls back from pli_005 in case the church baptism is not found.

Search the 1930 Mexico National Census (Ancestry collection 1771) for Mauro Cruz Corona and his parents. In 1930, Mauro would be approximately 20 years old and may still reside in the parental household in Coahuayutla or the Parácuaro area, directly confirming the parent-child relationship via co-residence. Even if Mauro has moved out, parents may appear with younger Cruz children. The 1930 census is the only major Mexican national census publicly available for this era. Ages and birthplaces recorded in the census can help confirm identity across records. This is a co-equal item (not a fallback) because it covers a different time point and a different evidence type from the birth/baptism searches.

Full-text co-occurrence search (to be executed via the search-full-text skill) for 'Cruz' AND 'Corona' as separate required terms, run unscoped across FamilySearch's AI-transcribed documents for Guerrero and Michoacán. Per the Mexico Naming Customs wiki: a child's baptism entry names the father as '[Father's given name] Cruz [father's maternal surname]' and the mother as '[Mother's given name] Corona [mother's maternal surname]' — the co-occurrence of both family surnames within a paragraph-style parish or civil register entry is a high-precision signal for Mauro's family unit. This tactic surfaces transcription variants and partially-indexed records that defeat name-indexed searches. Do not scope to a specific collection id. This is a fallback to deploy when indexed searches (pli_001 through pli_006) have been exhausted without finding Mauro's baptism or the parents' marriage.

Browse the Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (FamilySearch Catalog item 320251, 1637–1915) for the parents' marriage in the Parácuaro area. Per loc_001: 'Archdiocese of Michoacán ecclesiastical marriage investigation records (1637–1915) are at FamilySearch Catalog (catalog/320251) and may document parents' or grandparents' marriages predating civil registration.' These pre-sacramental investigation files (informaciones matrimoniales) routinely name both parties' parents, making them equivalent to a birth record for establishing grandparents' names. The collection ends 1915, covering the parents' likely marriage window. Date window: upper bound 1915 (collection end); lower bound 1895, assuming a parent born ca. 1875 and marrying in their late teens or early twenties. This item is a fallback for pli_003 in case the Guerrero church marriage search fails and the parents married in Michoacán rather than Guerrero.

entry.notes: Original Catholic baptismal register image. The index spells the mother's surname as 'Crona'; this is a known transcription variant of 'Corona' confirmed by the Liborio and Marcelino baptism records in the same collection which index the same woman as 'Apolinar Corona'. Child's surname also indexed as 'Cruz Crona' in the index.

entry.informant_bias_notes: The child's name was supplied by the presenting parents to the officiating priest at the baptism. The FamilySearch index renders the surname as 'Cruz Crona'; the correct form 'Cruz Corona' is confirmed by the record's own alternate name field and by sibling baptism records in the same collection.

The FamilySearch index standard place is 'San Agustín, Tlapa de Comonfort, Guerrero' — this is an index error; the image group metadata and record content place the church in Coahuayutla de Guerrero, not Tlapa de Comonfort.
The father's name was supplied by the presenting parents (including himself) to the priest at baptism. The father's own presence at the baptism is likely though not certain from the record alone.

The paternal relationship is explicitly stated in the baptismal register's father field. This record establishes that Sóstenes Cruz was the father of Facundo Cruz Corona — providing indirect evidence that Mauro Cruz Corona, believed to be a sibling, shared the same father.

The FamilySearch index renders the surname as 'Crona' — a known transcription variant of 'Corona' documented across this collection. The record's own alternate name field gives 'Apolinar Corona' and sibling baptism records (Liborio, Marcelino) in the same collection confirm the surname as 'Corona'. The corrected form is used here; the indexed variant 'Crona' is noted for awareness.

The maternal relationship is explicitly stated in the baptismal register's mother field. Mother's surname indexed as 'Crona' — corrected to 'Corona' per sibling baptism records and the record's alternate name field. This record provides indirect evidence that Mauro Cruz Corona shared Apolinar Corona as his mother.

- 004605080_020_M946-7DD: 1911-1913 baptisms (91% indexed, full-text searchable)

2. Add a new plan item specifically targeting the La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca baptism volumes for 1910-1913, via fulltext_search on the DGS volume numbers above. This is now the highest-priority item.
3. Assess pli_002-pli_009: recommend which should be executed (especially those that would provide independent verification of Mauro's parents or birth) and which can be skipped given what we've found. The overall goal is to get to a defensible GPS conclusion on both sub-questions: (1) parents [essentially answered] and (2) exact birth date and place [La Unión, Guerrero ~1912 from secondary evidence; need baptism for exact date].

All 4 records extracted cleanly — 51 assertions across sources S1–S4. Printing the researcher-facing summaries:

---

The 1918 baptismal register of San Agustín Catholic parish in Coahuayutla de Guerrero, Mexico records that a baby boy named Facundo Cruz Corona was baptized on 13 December 1918. The register names his father as Sóstenes Cruz and his mother as Apolinar Corona (the index misspells her surname as "Crona," but sibling baptism records in the same collection confirm the correct spelling is "Corona"). This is the same parish register image held at FamilySearch, so the classification is an original source with the priest as a firsthand witness to the baptism itself, and the parents as the firsthand sources for the family names they declared.

The next step is for the person-evidence skill to link the father (Sóstenes Cruz) and mother (Apolinar Corona) personas from this record to their tree persons, and then to correlate this baptism with the Liborio and Marcelino baptism records to build the independent corroboration needed to answer q_001 about Mauro Cruz Corona's parents.

---

The 1916 baptismal register of San Agustín parish in Coahuayutla de Guerrero records the baptism of Liborio Cruz Corona on 27 August 1916. The entry states he was born on 23 July (no year written), names his father as Sóstenes Cruz and his mother as Apolinar Corona, and locates the baptism at that parish. This is an original church register entry, and the priest's own recording of the ceremony makes it a strong source for the baptism date, the child's name, and the parents' names — though the birth year of approximately 1916 is inferred from the baptism date rather than stated outright.

The next step is for the person-evidence skill to link the Liborio and Sóstenes/Apolinar personas from this record to their counterparts in the tree.

---

The 1921 baptismal register of San Agustín church in Coahuayutla de Guerrero records that Marcelino Cruz Corona, a male child, was baptized on 15 May 1921, twenty days after his birth on 25 April. The register names his father as Sostenes Cruz and his mother as Apolinar Corona — the same couple who appear as parents in the other sibling baptism records from the same parish. The entry is an original church register, though the FamilySearch index mis-identifies the church's location as Tlapa de Comonfort; the image group metadata correctly places it in Coahuayutla de Guerrero.

The next step is for person-evidence to link Marcelino to a new tree entry and to connect Sostenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona to the existing parent-hypothesis being built for Mauro Cruz Corona under q_001.

---

In 1941, a Catholic parish in Michoacán, Mexico opened an official marriage investigation file — an "expediente matrimonial" — for Mauro Cruz and Esperanza Ramirez. As part of that process, Mauro gave a sworn declaration stating that he was twenty-nine years old, originally from La Unión in the state of Guerrero, had lived in Nueva Italia, Michoacán for approximately fourteen years, and was the legitimate son of Sóstenes Cruz, who had already died, and María Apolinar Corona, who was still living at the time. The ceremony itself took place on February 6, 1941, in Nueva Italia, though the paperwork was filed with the Parácuaro parish on February 20. Esperanza stated she was twenty-eight years old, from Tingambato, and the daughter of Mateo Ramirez and Carmen Martinez.

The next step is to link each of the six named individuals to their corresponding tree persons, and then to search for Mauro's baptismal record in La Unión, Guerrero, around 1911–1913, to corroborate the birthplace and narrow the birth date.

1 of 1 — Guerrero civil birth registration, Mauro Cruz Corona, 22 Nov 1910, La Unión.

This is the civil birth registration for Mauro Cruz Corona, recorded on 6 December 1910 at Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico. The record states that Mauro was born on 22 November 1910 in La Unión (now La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero), and names his father as Sóstenes Cruz and his mother as Apolinar Corona. The mother's surname appears with two characters obscured by OCR in the index, but four sibling birth registrations and Mauro's own 1941 marriage file all independently confirm "Corona" as her surname.

The next step is to view the original image of the registration (image ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V) to read the full handwritten text directly, then move toward a proof conclusion for the question of Mauro's parents and birth details.

The official birth record for Mauro Cruz, registered 6 December 1910 in La Unión, Guerrero, names his father as Sóstenes Cruz, age 30, a laborer from Coahuayutla living at Rincón de Cuchara, and his mother as Apolinar Corona, age 25, also from Coahuayutla.
